data.text: "ANG GALING NI SEC. VINCE" Muling nabuksan ang usapin sa kalidad ng EDSA rehabilitation project matapos maiulat na ilang bahagi ng kalsadang isinailalim sa road reblocking ay nagkaroon na agad ng mga lubak at pagkabakbak sa kabila ng kamakailang pagkakagawa nito. Batay sa ulat ng 24 Oras, kabilang sa mga apektadong lugar ang ilang seksyon ng EDSA Busway at mga bahagi ng Phase 1 ng road reblocking project na sinimulan noong bisperas ng Pasko noong nakaraang taon. Tinatayang aabot sa P1.2 bilyon ang halaga ng naturang proyekto. Dahil dito, binatikos ni veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza ang Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) sa ilalim ni Secretary Vince Dizon. Sa kanyang social media post, kinuwestiyon niya kung bakit nagkaroon agad ng sira ang ilang bahagi ng EDSA sa kabila ng malaking pondong inilaan para sa rehabilitasyon. Sa ngayon, wala pang inilalabas na pahayag si Dizon kaugnay sa mga batikos at sa ulat hinggil sa kondisyon ng ilang bagong inayos na bahagi ng pangunahing lansangan sa Metro Manila.

"SEC. VINCE IS GREAT"
The issue of the quality of the EDSA rehabilitation project has been reopened after it was reported that several sections of the road undergoing reblocking have already developed potholes and peeling despite having been recently completed.
According to a report from 24 Oras, affected areas include several sections of the EDSA Busway and parts of Phase 1 of the road reblocking project that started on Christmas Eve of last year.
The cost of the project is estimated to reach P1.2 billion.
As a result, veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza criticized the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) under Secretary Vince Dizon.
In his social media post, he questioned why certain parts of EDSA have damaged so quickly despite the large funds allocated for the rehabilitation.
As of now, Dizon has not issued any statement regarding the criticisms and the report about the condition of some newly repaired sections of the main thoroughfare in Metro Manila.

"SEC. VINCE IS GREAT"

In his social media post, he questioned why certain parts of EDSA have damaged so quickly despite the large funds allocated for the rehabilitation.
As of now, Dizon has not issued any statement regarding the criticisms and the report about the condition of some newly repaired sections of the main thoroughfare in Metro Manila.

input.source_text:
"ANG GALING NI SEC. VINCE" Muling nabuksan ang usapin sa kalidad ng EDSA rehabilitation project matapos maiulat na ilang bahagi ng kalsadang isinailalim sa road reblocking ay nagkaroon na agad ng mga lubak at pagkabakbak sa kabila ng kamakailang pagkakagawa nito. Batay sa ulat ng 24 Oras, kabilang sa mga apektadong lugar ang ilang seksyon ng EDSA Busway at mga bahagi ng Phase 1 ng road reblocking project na sinimulan noong bisperas ng Pasko noong nakaraang taon. Tinatayang aabot sa P1.2 bilyon ang halaga ng naturang proyekto. Dahil dito, binatikos ni veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza ang Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) sa ilalim ni Secretary Vince Dizon. Sa kanyang social media post, kinuwestiyon niya kung bakit nagkaroon agad ng sira ang ilang bahagi ng EDSA sa kabila ng malaking pondong inilaan para sa rehabilitasyon. Sa ngayon, wala pang inilalabas na pahayag si Dizon kaugnay sa mga batikos at sa ulat hinggil sa kondisyon ng ilang bagong inayos na bahagi ng pangunahing lansangan sa Metro Manila.
"SEC. VINCE IS GREAT"

According to a report from 24 Oras, affected areas include several sections of the EDSA Busway and parts of Phase 1 of the road reblocking project that started on Christmas Eve of last year.
The cost of the project is estimated to reach P1.2 billion.
As a result, veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza criticized the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) under Secretary Vince Dizon.
In his social media post, he questioned why certain parts of EDSA have damaged so quickly despite the large funds allocated for the rehabilitation.
As of now, Dizon has not issued any statement regarding the criticisms and the report about the condition of some newly repaired sections of the main thoroughfare in Metro Manila.

claim.evidence_context:
"SEC. VINCE IS GREAT"
The issue of the quality of the EDSA rehabilitation project has been reopened after it was reported that several sections of the road undergoing reblocking have already developed potholes and peeling despite having been recently completed.
According to a report from 24 Oras, affected areas include several sections of the EDSA Busway and parts of Phase 1 of the road reblocking project that started on Christmas Eve of last year.
The cost of the project is estimated to reach P1.2 billion.
As a result, veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza criticized the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) under Secretary Vince Dizon.
In his social media post, he questioned why certain parts of EDSA have damaged so quickly despite the large funds allocated for the rehabilitation.
As of now, Dizon has not issued any statement regarding the criticisms and the report about the condition of some newly repaired sections of the main thoroughfare in Metro Manila.

input.source_text:
"ANG GALING NI SEC. VINCE" Muling nabuksan ang usapin sa kalidad ng EDSA rehabilitation project matapos maiulat na ilang bahagi ng kalsadang isinailalim sa road reblocking ay nagkaroon na agad ng mga lubak at pagkabakbak sa kabila ng kamakailang pagkakagawa nito. Batay sa ulat ng 24 Oras, kabilang sa mga apektadong lugar ang ilang seksyon ng EDSA Busway at mga bahagi ng Phase 1 ng road reblocking project na sinimulan noong bisperas ng Pasko noong nakaraang taon. Tinatayang aabot sa P1.2 bilyon ang halaga ng naturang proyekto. Dahil dito, binatikos ni veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza ang Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) sa ilalim ni Secretary Vince Dizon. Sa kanyang social media post, kinuwestiyon niya kung bakit nagkaroon agad ng sira ang ilang bahagi ng EDSA sa kabila ng malaking pondong inilaan para sa rehabilitasyon. Sa ngayon, wala pang inilalabas na pahayag si Dizon kaugnay sa mga batikos at sa ulat hinggil sa kondisyon ng ilang bagong inayos na bahagi ng pangunahing lansangan sa Metro Manila.

"Buong stretch ng EDSA mula south hanggang Monumento lalaparan natin 'yung sidewalk para sa mga kababayan natin," Dizon said in an interview on Unang Balita after inspecting the EDSA-Buendia area. (On the whole stretch of EDSA from the south until Monumento, we will widen the sidewalk for our countrymen.) He also said the asphalt being used on EDSA is of good quality, at par with that being used in other countries like Japan and Korea. "Ongoing ang Phase 2 (ng EDSA rehabilitation) mula Guadalupe Orense hanggang Monumento. Ngayon nagtatrabaho tayo sa Monumento side. Kanina ininspeksiyon ko 'yung bandang Boni papunta ng Shaw Boulevard, nag-aayos na rin tayo diyan. By next year, tingin ko, tapos na ito," Dizon said. (Phase 2 [of EDSA rehabilitation] from Guadalupe Orense to Monumento is ongoing. We are working on the Monumento side. Earlier, I inspected the area [of EDSA] from Boni [Avenue] toward Shaw Boulevard as we are working there too. By next year, I think we will be finished.) "Last year naglakad kami dito with Sec. Banoy and nakita natin na kawawa talaga 'yung mga kababayan natin na nagco-commute at saka ang mga naglalakad. output.title: MMDA eyes P50,000 fine for EDSA rehab contractor over traffic jam
output.description: The MMDA wants the contractor of EDSA rehabilitation project to pay a fine over traffic disruption caused by road asphalt paving along EDSA Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard.
output.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) is seeking to impose a fine on the contractor of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program over the traffic disruption along EDSA from Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard on Sunday, August 23. In a statement on Monday, August 24, the MMDA said it is already coordinating with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to fine the contractor for allegedly failing to deploy flagmen in the area to manage traffic. The contractor could face a P50,000 fine over the violation, according to the agency. The traffic jam reportedly occurred during asphalt paving works in the area. Several sections of EDSA—a major thoroughfare that spans several cities in Metro Manila—have been undergoing rehabilitation and repair, while potholes emerged in newly rehabilitated portions following weeks of incessant heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat. The potholes formed after rainwater accumulated on the roads, according to the DPWH's initial assessment. Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the contractor to immediately repair the potholes at no cost to the government. Sen. Ping Lacson earlier called out the potholes on the newly repaired portions of EDSA and filed a resolution seeking a Senate inquiry into the rehabilitation project. The contract for Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program was awarded to Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. for P1.18 billion. The project covered Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and was completed in April 2026. Phase 2 was also awarded to Readycon in a joint venture with Dumduma Construction and Trading Corp. for P4 billion. It covers Orense Street to Monumento. output.title: Dizon welcomes possible probe on EDSA potholes | ABS-CBN News
output.description: The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the
output.text: MANILA — The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the appearance of potholes. In a statement, Secretary Vince Dizon said the agency welcomes the proposal, as legislative oversight is “essential to ensuring transparency and protecting public funds”. He also said he has directed the DPWH National Capital Region to compel the contractor to repair all affected sections of Phase 1 at zero cost to the government, as well as to address the causes of the problem. “We are auditing contractor compliance, and if our investigation reveals substandard workmanship or negligence, we will hold those responsible fully accountable,” Dizon said. “We stand ready to cooperate fully with the Senate Committee on Public Works. We share Senator Lacson’s resolve to ensure every peso spent on public infrastructure delivers the quality and safety Filipinos deserve,” he added. Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson earlier sought an investigation into the rehabilitation of EDSA after fresh potholes emerged on newly repaired portions of the highway following recent monsoon rains. Lacson’s Senate Resolution 594 directs the Senate Committee on Public Works to conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation to review design and engineering standards and ensure accountability in public infrastructure. output.title: SONA 2018 Promise Tracker: Infrastructure
output.description: The government’s P9-trillion Build, Build, Build program is now halfway to “revolutionizing” public infrastructures in the country, according to Public Works and Highways Secretary Mark Villar.

text.preview: By Ivel John M. Santos The government’s P9-trillion Build, Build, Build program is now halfway to “revolutionizing” public infrastructures in the country, according to Public Works and Highways Secretary Mark Villar. In 2018, new bridges and roads were built while construction and rehabilitation of airports continued. A third major player has joined the telecommunications industry to break the current duopoly of Smart Communications and Globe Telecom. In his second State of the Nation Address in 2017, Duterte said: “We will make the next few years the Golden Age of Infrastructure in the Philippines to enhance our mobility and connectivity and thereby spur equitable growth and development in the country.” In its latest report , the National Economic and Development Authority said the completion of 75 “game-changing and high-impact” flagship infrastructure projects of the government would have to wait until after the term of President Duterte. Twenty-five projects are expected to be finished by 2022 while the other 50 should be completed beyond 2022. As his administration moves into the second half of its six-year term, here is the list of promises presenting how he has fared in the infrastructure sector. The draft Terms of Reference (TOR) for the new major player in the telecommunications industry was released on July 28, 2018. In November 2018, the National Telecommunications Commission announced that Mindanao Islamic Telephone Co. (Mislatel) consortium, which has been renamed as Dito Telecommunity, will be the new major player in the telecommunication industry. Mislatel received its Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) on July 8, despite questions about its franchise and the ties of Mislatel Chair Dennis Uy to Duterte. articles.title: SONA 2018 Promise Tracker: Infrastructure
articles.description: The government’s P9-trillion Build, Build, Build program is now halfway to “revolutionizing” public infrastructures in the country, according to Public Works and Highways Secretary Mark Villar.

text.preview: By Ivel John M. Santos The government’s P9-trillion Build, Build, Build program is now halfway to “revolutionizing” public infrastructures in the country, according to Public Works and Highways Secretary Mark Villar. In 2018, new bridges and roads were built while construction and rehabilitation of airports continued. A third major player has joined the telecommunications industry to break the current duopoly of Smart Communications and Globe Telecom. In his second State of the Nation Address in 2017, Duterte said: “We will make the next few years the Golden Age of Infrastructure in the Philippines to enhance our mobility and connectivity and thereby spur equitable growth and development in the country.” In its latest report , the National Economic and Development Authority said the completion of 75 “game-changing and high-impact” flagship infrastructure projects of the government would have to wait until after the term of President Duterte. Twenty-five projects are expected to be finished by 2022 while the other 50 should be completed beyond 2022. As his administration moves into the second half of its six-year term, here is the list of promises presenting how he has fared in the infrastructure sector. The draft Terms of Reference (TOR) for the new major player in the telecommunications industry was released on July 28, 2018. In November 2018, the National Telecommunications Commission announced that Mindanao Islamic Telephone Co. (Mislatel) consortium, which has been renamed as Dito Telecommunity, will be the new major player in the telecommunication industry. Mislatel received its Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) on July 8, despite questions about its franchise and the ties of Mislatel Chair Dennis Uy to Duterte. Uy helped bankroll Duterte’s campaign in the 2016 presidential elections. Mislatel is committed to provide an internet speed of 55 Mbps covering 84.01% of the country. articles.title: Dizon welcomes possible probe on EDSA potholes | ABS-CBN News
articles.description: The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the
articles.text: MANILA — The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the appearance of potholes. In a statement, Secretary Vince Dizon said the agency welcomes the proposal, as legislative oversight is “essential to ensuring transparency and protecting public funds”. He also said he has directed the DPWH National Capital Region to compel the contractor to repair all affected sections of Phase 1 at zero cost to the government, as well as to address the causes of the problem. “We are auditing contractor compliance, and if our investigation reveals substandard workmanship or negligence, we will hold those responsible fully accountable,” Dizon said. “We stand ready to cooperate fully with the Senate Committee on Public Works. We share Senator Lacson’s resolve to ensure every peso spent on public infrastructure delivers the quality and safety Filipinos deserve,” he added. Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson earlier sought an investigation into the rehabilitation of EDSA after fresh potholes emerged on newly repaired portions of the highway following recent monsoon rains. Lacson’s Senate Resolution 594 directs the Senate Committee on Public Works to conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation to review design and engineering standards and ensure accountability in public infrastructure. articles.description: The MMDA wants the contractor of EDSA rehabilitation project to pay a fine over traffic disruption caused by road asphalt paving along EDSA Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard.
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) is seeking to impose a fine on the contractor of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program over the traffic disruption along EDSA from Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard on Sunday, August 23. In a statement on Monday, August 24, the MMDA said it is already coordinating with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to fine the contractor for allegedly failing to deploy flagmen in the area to manage traffic. The contractor could face a P50,000 fine over the violation, according to the agency. The traffic jam reportedly occurred during asphalt paving works in the area. Several sections of EDSA—a major thoroughfare that spans several cities in Metro Manila—have been undergoing rehabilitation and repair, while potholes emerged in newly rehabilitated portions following weeks of incessant heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat. The potholes formed after rainwater accumulated on the roads, according to the DPWH's initial assessment. Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the contractor to immediately repair the potholes at no cost to the government. Sen. Ping Lacson earlier called out the potholes on the newly repaired portions of EDSA and filed a resolution seeking a Senate inquiry into the rehabilitation project. The contract for Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program was awarded to Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. for P1.18 billion. The project covered Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and was completed in April 2026. Phase 2 was also awarded to Readycon in a joint venture with Dumduma Construction and Trading Corp. for P4 billion. It covers Orense Street to Monumento. articles.title: Dizon welcomes possible probe on EDSA potholes | ABS-CBN News
articles.description: The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the
articles.text: MANILA — The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the appearance of potholes. In a statement, Secretary Vince Dizon said the agency welcomes the proposal, as legislative oversight is “essential to ensuring transparency and protecting public funds”. He also said he has directed the DPWH National Capital Region to compel the contractor to repair all affected sections of Phase 1 at zero cost to the government, as well as to address the causes of the problem. “We are auditing contractor compliance, and if our investigation reveals substandard workmanship or negligence, we will hold those responsible fully accountable,” Dizon said. “We stand ready to cooperate fully with the Senate Committee on Public Works. We share Senator Lacson’s resolve to ensure every peso spent on public infrastructure delivers the quality and safety Filipinos deserve,” he added. Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson earlier sought an investigation into the rehabilitation of EDSA after fresh potholes emerged on newly repaired portions of the highway following recent monsoon rains. Lacson’s Senate Resolution 594 directs the Senate Committee on Public Works to conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation to review design and engineering standards and ensure accountability in public infrastructure. articles.title: MMDA eyes P50,000 fine for EDSA rehab contractor over traffic jam
articles.description: The MMDA wants the contractor of EDSA rehabilitation project to pay a fine over traffic disruption caused by road asphalt paving along EDSA Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard.
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) is seeking to impose a fine on the contractor of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program over the traffic disruption along EDSA from Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard on Sunday, August 23. In a statement on Monday, August 24, the MMDA said it is already coordinating with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to fine the contractor for allegedly failing to deploy flagmen in the area to manage traffic. The contractor could face a P50,000 fine over the violation, according to the agency. The traffic jam reportedly occurred during asphalt paving works in the area. Several sections of EDSA—a major thoroughfare that spans several cities in Metro Manila—have been undergoing rehabilitation and repair, while potholes emerged in newly rehabilitated portions following weeks of incessant heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat. The potholes formed after rainwater accumulated on the roads, according to the DPWH's initial assessment. Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the contractor to immediately repair the potholes at no cost to the government. Sen. Ping Lacson earlier called out the potholes on the newly repaired portions of EDSA and filed a resolution seeking a Senate inquiry into the rehabilitation project. The contract for Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program was awarded to Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. for P1.18 billion. The project covered Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and was completed in April 2026. Phase 2 was also awarded to Readycon in a joint venture with Dumduma Construction and Trading Corp. for P4 billion. It covers Orense Street to Monumento. text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — A resolution seeking an investigation into EDSA's rehabilitation and repair was filed on Thursday, August 13, after potholes emerged following more than a week of heavy rains in Metro Manila. Senate Resolution No. 594, filed by Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, asked the Senate Committee on Public Works to assess the EDSA Rehabilitation Project and review its design and engineering standards. Lacson cited the P6 billion budget allocated for the rehabilitation and repair of EDSA in the resolution, adding that the investigation is intended to ensure accountability. On August 10, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon inspected the EDSA Busway along Estrella Street in Makati City after potholes appeared in the area. He said the damage was caused by rainwater. The affected roads are part of Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Project. “For nearly a week, persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) rains have drenched parts of Luzon, including Metro Manila; damaging several main thoroughfares, including recently rehabilitated sections of EDSA. The presence of fresh potholes means the newly repaired avenue will already require another round of maintenance,” the resolution reads. The project was launched by the Department of Public Works and Highways in June 2025, with Phase 1 covering the repair of Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and Phase 2 covering Orense Street to Monumento. Both rehabilitation and repair projects were awarded to Readycon Trading & Construction Corp., with the second phase a joint venture with Dumduma Construction & Trading Corp. articles.title: SONA 2024 PROMISE TRACKER: Infrastructure
articles.description: Midway through his term, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. remains committed to delivering infrastructure projects “with a heart for people’s comfort, security, and progress.” However, the same challenges continue to hound his administration’s pursuit of “building better more.”

text.preview: Midway through his term, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. remains committed to delivering infrastructure projects “with a heart for people’s comfort, security, and progress.” However, the same challenges continue to hound his administration’s pursuit of “building better more.” Of the president’s 16 promises in infrastructure during his first three State of the Nation Addresses, only three have been fulfilled, 10 remain in progress and three were stalled. As of June 2025, the administration has 207 Infrastructure Flagship Projects (IFPs) worth US$178 billion. Eight of these have been completed, 70 are ongoing and 23 are approved for implementation. The rest are either awaiting government approval, under the preparation stage or still in the pre-project preparation phase. In addition to the IFPs, the administration also has 3,224 infrastructure projects under the Philippine Development Plan’s 2023-2028 Public Investment Program amounting to US$ 225.1 billion. One of the big-ticket projects accomplished in 2024 is the Panguil Bay Bridge, the longest sea-crossing bridge in Mindanao. Other completed IFPs include the Expanded Plaridel Bypass Road inaugurated in October 2024 and the Samar Coastal Road Project that opened in 2023. Last November, Marcos also inaugurated the LRT-1 Cavite Extension Project Phase 1 that traverses Parañaque City and Quezon City. In 2024, the overall infrastructure disbursements were recorded at P1.55 trillion. This is equivalent to 5.8% of gross domestic product hitting last year’s target of 5.0 to 6.0%. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) also saw improvements in the country’s fixed and mobile broadband speed between January 2023 to March 2025. Despite these wins, several of the administration’s infrastructure projects face delays due to problems in Right-of-Way (ROW) acquisitions and funding. articles.title: SONA 2024 PROMISE TRACKER: Infrastructure
articles.description: Midway through his term, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. remains committed to delivering infrastructure projects “with a heart for people’s comfort, security, and progress.” However, the same challenges continue to hound his administration’s pursuit of “building better more.”

text.preview: Midway through his term, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. remains committed to delivering infrastructure projects “with a heart for people’s comfort, security, and progress.” However, the same challenges continue to hound his administration’s pursuit of “building better more.” Of the president’s 16 promises in infrastructure during his first three State of the Nation Addresses, only three have been fulfilled, 10 remain in progress and three were stalled. As of June 2025, the administration has 207 Infrastructure Flagship Projects (IFPs) worth US$178 billion. Eight of these have been completed, 70 are ongoing and 23 are approved for implementation. The rest are either awaiting government approval, under the preparation stage or still in the pre-project preparation phase. In addition to the IFPs, the administration also has 3,224 infrastructure projects under the Philippine Development Plan’s 2023-2028 Public Investment Program amounting to US$ 225.1 billion. One of the big-ticket projects accomplished in 2024 is the Panguil Bay Bridge, the longest sea-crossing bridge in Mindanao. Other completed IFPs include the Expanded Plaridel Bypass Road inaugurated in October 2024 and the Samar Coastal Road Project that opened in 2023. Last November, Marcos also inaugurated the LRT-1 Cavite Extension Project Phase 1 that traverses Parañaque City and Quezon City. In 2024, the overall infrastructure disbursements were recorded at P1.55 trillion. This is equivalent to 5.8% of gross domestic product hitting last year’s target of 5.0 to 6.0%. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) also saw improvements in the country’s fixed and mobile broadband speed between January 2023 to March 2025. Despite these wins, several of the administration’s infrastructure projects face delays due to problems in Right-of-Way (ROW) acquisitions and funding. Twenty-five projects are expected to be finished by 2022 while the other 50 should be completed beyond 2022. articles.description: The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the
articles.text: MANILA — The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the appearance of potholes. In a statement, Secretary Vince Dizon said the agency welcomes the proposal, as legislative oversight is “essential to ensuring transparency and protecting public funds”. He also said he has directed the DPWH National Capital Region to compel the contractor to repair all affected sections of Phase 1 at zero cost to the government, as well as to address the causes of the problem. “We are auditing contractor compliance, and if our investigation reveals substandard workmanship or negligence, we will hold those responsible fully accountable,” Dizon said. “We stand ready to cooperate fully with the Senate Committee on Public Works. We share Senator Lacson’s resolve to ensure every peso spent on public infrastructure delivers the quality and safety Filipinos deserve,” he added. Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson earlier sought an investigation into the rehabilitation of EDSA after fresh potholes emerged on newly repaired portions of the highway following recent monsoon rains. Lacson’s Senate Resolution 594 directs the Senate Committee on Public Works to conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation to review design and engineering standards and ensure accountability in public infrastructure. article.text: MANILA — The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the appearance of potholes. article.description: Midway through his term, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. remains committed to delivering infrastructure projects “with a heart for people’s comfort, security, and progress.” However, the same challenges continue to hound his administration’s pursuit of “building better more.”

As of June 2025, the administration has 207 Infrastructure Flagship Projects (IFPs) worth US$178 billion. Eight of these have been completed, 70 are ongoing and 23 are approved for implementation. The rest are either awaiting government approval, under the preparation stage or still in the pre-project preparation phase. In addition to the IFPs, the administration also has 3,224 infrastructure projects under the Philippine Development Plan’s 2023-2028 Public Investment Program amounting to US$ 225.1 billion. One of the big-ticket projects accomplished in 2024 is the Panguil Bay Bridge, the longest sea-crossing bridge in Mindanao. Other completed IFPs include the Expanded Plaridel Bypass Road inaugurated in October 2024 and the Samar Coastal Road Project that opened in 2023. Last November, Marcos also inaugurated the LRT-1 Cavite Extension Project Phase 1 that traverses Parañaque City and Quezon City. In 2024, the overall infrastructure disbursements were recorded at P1.55 trillion. This is equivalent to 5.8% of gross domestic product hitting last year’s target of 5.0 to 6.0%. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) also saw improvements in the country’s fixed and mobile broadband speed between January 2023 to March 2025. article.description: Commuters may expect wider sidewalks and motorists will have a smoother ride throughout EDSA once its rehabilitation is finished by next year, Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon said Monday.

text.preview: Commuters may expect wider sidewalks and motorists will have a smoother ride throughout EDSA once its rehabilitation is finished by next year, Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon said Monday. "Buong stretch ng EDSA mula south hanggang Monumento lalaparan natin 'yung sidewalk para sa mga kababayan natin," Dizon said in an interview on Unang Balita after inspecting the EDSA-Buendia area. (On the whole stretch of EDSA from the south until Monumento, we will widen the sidewalk for our countrymen.) He also said the asphalt being used on EDSA is of good quality, at par with that being used in other countries like Japan and Korea. "Ongoing ang Phase 2 (ng EDSA rehabilitation) mula Guadalupe Orense hanggang Monumento. Ngayon nagtatrabaho tayo sa Monumento side. Kanina ininspeksiyon ko 'yung bandang Boni papunta ng Shaw Boulevard, nag-aayos na rin tayo diyan. By next year, tingin ko, tapos na ito," Dizon said. (Phase 2 [of EDSA rehabilitation] from Guadalupe Orense to Monumento is ongoing. We are working on the Monumento side. Earlier, I inspected the area [of EDSA] from Boni [Avenue] toward Shaw Boulevard as we are working there too. By next year, I think we will be finished.) article.title: EDSA road repair causes traffic congestion; DPWH eyes more permanent solution
article.description: Repairs on EDSA that began Friday night has led to traffic build-up on Saturday. The Department of Public Works and Highways meanwhile said it is planning a long-term solution.

text.preview: Repairs on EDSA that began Friday night has led to traffic build-up on Saturday. The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) meanwhile said it is planning a long-term solution. On Saturday morning, the traffic build-up on the northbound lane stretched from North Avenue to just before the Quezon Avenue flyover in Quezon City. Aside from the repair of the EDSA Bus Carousel and portions of the main thoroughfare, workmen constructing the MRT7 common station were putting a girder using a crane truck, rendering only one lane passable, according to a report of Luisito Santos on Super Radyo dzBB. article.title: MMDA eyes P50,000 fine for EDSA rehab contractor over traffic jam
article.description: The MMDA wants the contractor of EDSA rehabilitation project to pay a fine over traffic disruption caused by road asphalt paving along EDSA Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard.
article.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) is seeking to impose a fine on the contractor of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program over the traffic disruption along EDSA from Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard on Sunday, August 23. In a statement on Monday, August 24, the MMDA said it is already coordinating with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to fine the contractor for allegedly failing to deploy flagmen in the area to manage traffic. The contractor could face a P50,000 fine over the violation, according to the agency. The traffic jam reportedly occurred during asphalt paving works in the area. Several sections of EDSA—a major thoroughfare that spans several cities in Metro Manila—have been undergoing rehabilitation and repair, while potholes emerged in newly rehabilitated portions following weeks of incessant heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat. The potholes formed after rainwater accumulated on the roads, according to the DPWH's initial assessment. Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the contractor to immediately repair the potholes at no cost to the government. Sen. Ping Lacson earlier called out the potholes on the newly repaired portions of EDSA and filed a resolution seeking a Senate inquiry into the rehabilitation project. The contract for Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program was awarded to Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. for P1.18 billion. The project covered Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and was completed in April 2026. Phase 2 was also awarded to Readycon in a joint venture with Dumduma Construction and Trading Corp. for P4 billion. It covers Orense Street to Monumento. article.title: Senate urged to probe EDSA repairs after potholes emerge
article.description: A resolution seeking an investigation into EDSA's rehabilitation and repair was filed on Thursday, August 13, after potholes emerged following more than a week of heavy rains in Metro Manila

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — A resolution seeking an investigation into EDSA's rehabilitation and repair was filed on Thursday, August 13, after potholes emerged following more than a week of heavy rains in Metro Manila. Senate Resolution No. 594, filed by Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, asked the Senate Committee on Public Works to assess the EDSA Rehabilitation Project and review its design and engineering standards. Lacson cited the P6 billion budget allocated for the rehabilitation and repair of EDSA in the resolution, adding that the investigation is intended to ensure accountability. On August 10, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon inspected the EDSA Busway along Estrella Street in Makati City after potholes appeared in the area. He said the damage was caused by rainwater. The affected roads are part of Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Project. “For nearly a week, persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) rains have drenched parts of Luzon, including Metro Manila; damaging several main thoroughfares, including recently rehabilitated sections of EDSA. The presence of fresh potholes means the newly repaired avenue will already require another round of maintenance,” the resolution reads. The project was launched by the Department of Public Works and Highways in June 2025, with Phase 1 covering the repair of Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and Phase 2 covering Orense Street to Monumento. Both rehabilitation and repair projects were awarded to Readycon Trading & Construction Corp., with the second phase a joint venture with Dumduma Construction & Trading Corp. The project’s Phase 1, completed in April 2026, was worth P1,183,374,622.61. articles.title: Dizon welcomes possible probe on EDSA potholes | ABS-CBN News
articles.description: The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the
articles.text: MANILA — The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the appearance of potholes. In a statement, Secretary Vince Dizon said the agency welcomes the proposal, as legislative oversight is “essential to ensuring transparency and protecting public funds”. He also said he has directed the DPWH National Capital Region to compel the contractor to repair all affected sections of Phase 1 at zero cost to the government, as well as to address the causes of the problem. “We are auditing contractor compliance, and if our investigation reveals substandard workmanship or negligence, we will hold those responsible fully accountable,” Dizon said. “We stand ready to cooperate fully with the Senate Committee on Public Works. We share Senator Lacson’s resolve to ensure every peso spent on public infrastructure delivers the quality and safety Filipinos deserve,” he added. Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson earlier sought an investigation into the rehabilitation of EDSA after fresh potholes emerged on newly repaired portions of the highway following recent monsoon rains. Lacson’s Senate Resolution 594 directs the Senate Committee on Public Works to conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation to review design and engineering standards and ensure accountability in public infrastructure. articles.description: Repairs on EDSA that began Friday night has led to traffic build-up on Saturday. The Department of Public Works and Highways meanwhile said it is planning a long-term solution.

On Saturday morning, the traffic build-up on the northbound lane stretched from North Avenue to just before the Quezon Avenue flyover in Quezon City. Aside from the repair of the EDSA Bus Carousel and portions of the main thoroughfare, workmen constructing the MRT7 common station were putting a girder using a crane truck, rendering only one lane passable, according to a report of Luisito Santos on Super Radyo dzBB. articles.title: MMDA eyes P50,000 fine for EDSA rehab contractor over traffic jam
articles.description: The MMDA wants the contractor of EDSA rehabilitation project to pay a fine over traffic disruption caused by road asphalt paving along EDSA Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard.
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) is seeking to impose a fine on the contractor of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program over the traffic disruption along EDSA from Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard on Sunday, August 23. In a statement on Monday, August 24, the MMDA said it is already coordinating with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to fine the contractor for allegedly failing to deploy flagmen in the area to manage traffic. The contractor could face a P50,000 fine over the violation, according to the agency. The traffic jam reportedly occurred during asphalt paving works in the area. Several sections of EDSA—a major thoroughfare that spans several cities in Metro Manila—have been undergoing rehabilitation and repair, while potholes emerged in newly rehabilitated portions following weeks of incessant heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat. The potholes formed after rainwater accumulated on the roads, according to the DPWH's initial assessment. Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the contractor to immediately repair the potholes at no cost to the government. Sen. Ping Lacson earlier called out the potholes on the newly repaired portions of EDSA and filed a resolution seeking a Senate inquiry into the rehabilitation project. The contract for Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program was awarded to Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. for P1.18 billion. The project covered Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and was completed in April 2026. Phase 2 was also awarded to Readycon in a joint venture with Dumduma Construction and Trading Corp. for P4 billion. It covers Orense Street to Monumento. articles.description: A resolution seeking an investigation into EDSA's rehabilitation and repair was filed on Thursday, August 13, after potholes emerged following more than a week of heavy rains in Metro Manila

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — A resolution seeking an investigation into EDSA's rehabilitation and repair was filed on Thursday, August 13, after potholes emerged following more than a week of heavy rains in Metro Manila. Senate Resolution No. 594, filed by Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, asked the Senate Committee on Public Works to assess the EDSA Rehabilitation Project and review its design and engineering standards. Lacson cited the P6 billion budget allocated for the rehabilitation and repair of EDSA in the resolution, adding that the investigation is intended to ensure accountability. On August 10, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon inspected the EDSA Busway along Estrella Street in Makati City after potholes appeared in the area. He said the damage was caused by rainwater. The affected roads are part of Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Project. “For nearly a week, persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) rains have drenched parts of Luzon, including Metro Manila; damaging several main thoroughfares, including recently rehabilitated sections of EDSA. The presence of fresh potholes means the newly repaired avenue will already require another round of maintenance,” the resolution reads. The project was launched by the Department of Public Works and Highways in June 2025, with Phase 1 covering the repair of Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and Phase 2 covering Orense Street to Monumento. Both rehabilitation and repair projects were awarded to Readycon Trading & Construction Corp., with the second phase a joint venture with Dumduma Construction & Trading Corp. passages.text: Midway through his term, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. remains committed to delivering infrastructure projects “with a heart for people’s comfort, security, and progress.”
However, the same challenges continue to hound his administration’s pursuit of “building better more.”
Of the president’s 16 promises in infrastructure during his first three State of the Nation Addresses, only three have been fulfilled, 10 remain in progress and three were stalled.
As of June 2025, the administration has 207 Infrastructure Flagship Projects (IFPs) worth US$178 billion.
Eight of these have been completed, 70 are ongoing and 23 are approved for implementation.
The rest are either awaiting government approval, under the preparation stage or still in the pre-project preparation phase.
In addition to the IFPs, the administration also has 3,224 infrastructure projects under the Philippine Development Plan’s 2023-2028 Public Investment Program amounting to US$ 225.1 billion.
One of the big-ticket projects accomplished in 2024 is the Panguil Bay Bridge, the longest sea-crossing bridge in Mindanao.
Other completed IFPs include the Expanded Plaridel Bypass Road inaugurated in October 2024 and the Samar Coastal Road Project that opened in 2023.
Last November, Marcos also inaugurated the LRT-1 Cavite Extension Project Phase 1 that traverses Parañaque City and Quezon City.
In 2024, the overall infrastructure disbursements were recorded at P1.55 trillion.
This is equivalent to 5.8% of gross domestic product hitting last year’s target of 5.0 to 6.0%.
The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) also saw improvements in the country’s fixed and mobile broadband speed between January 2023 to March 2025.
Despite these wins, several of the administration’s infrastructure projects face delays due to problems in Right-of-Way (ROW) acquisitions and funding.

According to a February 2025 Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS) report, the country is lagging behind its Southeast Asian neighbors when it comes to transport infrastructure development, citing its inefficient air transport systems and “relatively underdeveloped” railways.

Notably, big-ticket infrastructure projects under the Department of Transportation (DOTr) such as the North-South Commuter Railway System, Metro Manila Subway Project and the MRT-7 were held up because of ROW acquisition disputes.
Other projects, such as the Mindanao Railway project, were also stalled due to lack of funding.
The World Bank, which is financing the Cebu Bus Rapid Transit Project, also rated the program’s overall implementation as “unsatisfactory” for its slow progress.
In his first three years, Marcos tried several measures to resolve the delays.
These include the creation of an inter-agency committee for rail projects with ROW concerns and the streamlining of processes for IFPs.

Most recently, Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon issued a department order creating the Flagship Project Management Office that aims to fast-track the implementation of priority transportation infrastructure programs.
With his first three years nearly over, Marcos now has the same amount of time left to deliver on his ambitious infrastructure agenda.

See how the president fared in his 2024 SONA promises on infrastructure here: “Our power and internet services are continuously being upgraded in both capacity and connectivity… Together with our private sector partners, we will efficiently harness the concept of common towers to provide connectivity to Filipinos who are at the far end of the last mile. Expect full government support to ensure the successful completion of this critical project, including policy reforms and streamlined processes.”

This is a repeat promise from SONA 2023 “The C-LEX, NLEX-SLEX Connector, and the Plaridel Bypass will be fully completed by the end of this year. CALAX and the C5 South Link will be fully operational by next year.”

“Under our Inter-Island Linkage Bridge Program, we expect two major bridges to be opened to motorists this year. One is the Panguil Bay Bridge — touted as the longest water-spanning bridge in Northern Mindanao. This bridge will connect Lanao del Norte to Misamis Occidental. The other is the Guicam Bridge in Zamboanga Sibugay, which shall connect Olutanga Island to the mainland of Mindanao.”

“We are in the midst as well of a ‘railway renaissance’. The Metro Manila Subway Project has logged significant accomplishments in its tunneling works. Other railway projects, such as the MRT-7 and the North- South Commuter Railway, are likewise progressing.”

This is a repeat promise from SONA 2022 “We will make sure that the right of way issues are resolved in the most equitable, efficient, and expeditious manner, so that these will not get in the way of our infrastructure development.”

“Bilang bahagi ng LRT 1 Cavite Extension project, ang ruta ng LRT Line 1 sa Metro Manila ay madadagdagan mula Baclaran hanggang Sucat. Bubuksan ito sa publiko sa loob ng taong ito. At sa ilang taon, aabot na ang linyang ito hanggang Bacoor.”

“Unang-una na rito ay ang Paliparan ng Maynila. Sa pangangasiwa ng pribadong sektor, inaasahang gaganda ang hitsura at serbisyo nito sa mga susunod na taon. Soon, it will be capable of accommodating 48 flights per hour, servicing our ever-increasing local and international flight routes, and catering to more than 62 million passengers per year.”

This is a repeat promise from SONA 2022 “More than seventy airport and seaport development projects across the country have been completed, and another 350 ongoing projects are set to be completed by 2028.”

“The approval of energy projects is moving towards complete virtual integration of its required procedures. The expedited processing of our infrastructure flagship projects under the Build Better More program shall also follow suit.”

He said reducing by 250,000 to 300,000 the number of cars passing through EDSA will help “revert the traffic to an acceptable level.”
Among the traffic-solution projects are Skyway, NLEX Harbor Link, and NLEX-SLEX Connector Road.
Villar said the Skyway Stage 3 project connecting Makati and Quezon City will open in July 2019.
He backed Duterte’s recent controversial statement that a five-minute travel time from Makati to Quezon City is possible through the Skyway.
The Philippine Government was able to secure multi-billion grants from China for the construction of two bridges along the Pasig River in Metro Manila in 2017.
These Chinese-funded bridges are the Binondo-Intramuros Bridge in Manila and the Estrella-Pantaleon Bridge between Mandaluyong and Makati, which are expected to be completed by 2021.
The Duterte administration has already built and repaired 2,709 bridges, connecting different parts of the country.
Among the bridges already completed are the Anduyan Bridge in La Union, Laoag City Bypass Bridge, and the Matampay Bridge in Cotabato City.
The government plans to build 17 short- and long-span bridges that will connect the islands of the country.

Among these inter-island projects are three Tawi-Tawi bridges, Bataan-Cavite Interlink Bridge, Sorsogon-Samar Link Bridge, Panguil Bay Bridge, and the Panglao-Tagbilaran City Offshore Connector Bridge.

The Duterte administration has already finished the construction of two new international airports: Lal-Lo International Airport (formerly Cagayan North International Airport) in Cagayan and the Bohol-Panglao International Airport.
These two airport projects started before Duterte’s term.
Chinese firms have been reportedly financing the expansion and construction of airports in the country such as of the Lal-Lo International Airport and the Sangley Airport in Cavite.
TheP735.6-billion New Manila International Airport in Bulacan is being eyed to help decongest the Ninoy Aquino International Airport.
The new airport is anticipated to be operational within “four to six years” from the target start of construction in 2020.

“The National Government Portal, which we launched recently, will allow faster and easier delivery of public services and reduce the number of visits of the public to agencies for government transactions.”

Among NGP’s features is a curated list of direct links to various online government services such as the processing of requests for birth certificates from the Philippine Statistical Authority (PSA).

As one of the three “e-government” flagship projects of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), the NGP is being designed to aggregate all government online resources and services in a single site.
Its completion is expected in 2022, according to the 2019 NGP Project Implementation Plan.
The National Broadband Plan (NBP) is still in progress following its rollout in 2017 upon consultations with stakeholders of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT).

The NBP was designed as the “blueprint” in establishing infostructures (portmanteau of information structures) in the country to fast-track the deployment of fiber optic cables and wireless technologies, and improve the reliability and affordability of internet.
The NBP has successfully tested and surveyed 100% of the dark fiber, or the unused fiber optic cables, in Mindanao, 90% in Visayas and 60% in Luzon.

for the expansion of fiber reach and enabling of medium and small Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to offer service to the public through open access facilities.
The government has also sealed 21 memoranda of understanding with Common Tower Providers for the acceleration of rehabilitation and establishment of communication towers.
Villar said the start of the operation of the cable landing and repeater signal stations in July is expected to increase the capacity of internet bandwidth in the Philippines to two terabytes.
The NBP aims to link more than 600 government agencies by 2019 and 2020 for a faster government transaction.
“We have installed free Wi-Fi Internet in almost 400 public places around the country. We hope that the public will use to access important information and services.”

As of June 2025, the administration has 207 Infrastructure Flagship Projects (IFPs) worth US$178 billion. Eight of these have been completed, 70 are ongoing and 23 are approved for implementation. In addition to the IFPs, the administration also has 3,224 infrastructure projects under the Philippine Development Plan’s 2023-2028 Public Investment Program amounting to US$ 225.1 billion. articles.text: MANILA — The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the appearance of potholes. In a statement, Secretary Vince Dizon said the agency welcomes the proposal, as legislative oversight is “essential to ensuring transparency and protecting public funds”. He also said he has directed the DPWH National Capital Region to compel the contractor to repair all affected sections of Phase 1 at zero cost to the government, as well as to address the causes of the problem. “We are auditing contractor compliance, and if our investigation reveals substandard workmanship or negligence, we will hold those responsible fully accountable,” Dizon said. “We stand ready to cooperate fully with the Senate Committee on Public Works. We share Senator Lacson’s resolve to ensure every peso spent on public infrastructure delivers the quality and safety Filipinos deserve,” he added. Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson earlier sought an investigation into the rehabilitation of EDSA after fresh potholes emerged on newly repaired portions of the highway following recent monsoon rains. Lacson’s Senate Resolution 594 directs the Senate Committee on Public Works to conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation to review design and engineering standards and ensure accountability in public infrastructure. articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) is seeking to impose a fine on the contractor of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program over the traffic disruption along EDSA from Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard on Sunday, August 23. In a statement on Monday, August 24, the MMDA said it is already coordinating with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to fine the contractor for allegedly failing to deploy flagmen in the area to manage traffic. The contractor could face a P50,000 fine over the violation, according to the agency. The traffic jam reportedly occurred during asphalt paving works in the area. Several sections of EDSA—a major thoroughfare that spans several cities in Metro Manila—have been undergoing rehabilitation and repair, while potholes emerged in newly rehabilitated portions following weeks of incessant heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat. The potholes formed after rainwater accumulated on the roads, according to the DPWH's initial assessment. Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the contractor to immediately repair the potholes at no cost to the government. Sen. Ping Lacson earlier called out the potholes on the newly repaired portions of EDSA and filed a resolution seeking a Senate inquiry into the rehabilitation project. The contract for Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program was awarded to Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. for P1.18 billion. The project covered Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and was completed in April 2026. Phase 2 was also awarded to Readycon in a joint venture with Dumduma Construction and Trading Corp. for P4 billion. It covers Orense Street to Monumento. "SEC. VINCE IS GREAT"
The issue of the quality of the EDSA rehabilitation project has been reopened after it was reported that several sections of the road undergoing reblocking have already developed potholes and peeling despite having been recently completed.
According to a report from 24 Oras, affected areas include several sections of the EDSA Busway and parts of Phase 1 of the road reblocking project that started on Christmas Eve of last year.
The cost of the project is estimated to reach P1.2 billion.
As a result, veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza criticized the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) under Secretary Vince Dizon.
In his social media post, he questioned why certain parts of EDSA have damaged so quickly despite the large funds allocated for the rehabilitation.
As of now, Dizon has not issued any statement regarding the criticisms and the report about the condition of some newly repaired sections of the main thoroughfare in Metro Manila.

passages.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) is seeking to impose a fine on the contractor of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program over the traffic disruption along EDSA from Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard on Sunday, August 23.

In a statement on Monday, August 24, the MMDA said it is already coordinating with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to fine the contractor for allegedly failing to deploy flagmen in the area to manage traffic.
The contractor could face a P50,000 fine over the violation, according to the agency.
The traffic jam reportedly occurred during asphalt paving works in the area.

Several sections of EDSA—a major thoroughfare that spans several cities in Metro Manila—have been undergoing rehabilitation and repair, while potholes emerged in newly rehabilitated portions following weeks of incessant heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat.
The potholes formed after rainwater accumulated on the roads, according to the DPWH's initial assessment.
Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the contractor to immediately repair the potholes at no cost to the government.
Sen. Ping Lacson earlier called out the potholes on the newly repaired portions of EDSA and filed a resolution seeking a Senate inquiry into the rehabilitation project.
The contract for Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program was awarded to Readycon Trading and Construction Corp.
for P1.18 billion.
The project covered Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and was completed in April 2026.
Phase 2 was also awarded to Readycon in a joint venture with Dumduma Construction and Trading Corp.
for P4 billion.
It covers Orense Street to Monumento.

MANILA, Philippines — A resolution seeking an investigation into EDSA's rehabilitation and repair was filed on Thursday, August 13, after potholes emerged following more than a week of heavy rains in Metro Manila.
Senate Resolution No. 594, filed by Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, asked the Senate Committee on Public Works to assess the EDSA Rehabilitation Project and review its design and engineering standards.
Lacson cited the P6 billion budget allocated for the rehabilitation and repair of EDSA in the resolution, adding that the investigation is intended to ensure accountability.
On August 10, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon inspected the EDSA Busway along Estrella Street in Makati City after potholes appeared in the area.
He said the damage was caused by rainwater.
The affected roads are part of Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Project.

“For nearly a week, persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) rains have drenched parts of Luzon, including Metro Manila; damaging several main thoroughfares, including recently rehabilitated sections of EDSA. The presence of fresh potholes means the newly repaired avenue will already require another round of maintenance,” the resolution reads.

The project was launched by the Department of Public Works and Highways in June 2025, with Phase 1 covering the repair of Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and Phase 2 covering Orense Street to Monumento.
Both rehabilitation and repair projects were awarded to Readycon Trading & Construction Corp., with the second phase a joint venture with Dumduma Construction & Trading Corp.
The project’s Phase 1, completed in April 2026, was worth P1,183,374,622.61.
Meanwhile, the Phase 2 contract, worth P4,009,473,018.88, was signed on June 4, with the Notice to Proceed issued on June 8, 2026.

“Rapid deterioration of recently rehabilitated roads, most notably EDSA, just months after completion exposes deep-seated flaws in the planning, design, construction and management of high-cost public infrastructure projects,” Lacson added.

articles.text: MANILA — The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the appearance of potholes. In a statement, Secretary Vince Dizon said the agency welcomes the proposal, as legislative oversight is “essential to ensuring transparency and protecting public funds”. He also said he has directed the DPWH National Capital Region to compel the contractor to repair all affected sections of Phase 1 at zero cost to the government, as well as to address the causes of the problem. “We are auditing contractor compliance, and if our investigation reveals substandard workmanship or negligence, we will hold those responsible fully accountable,” Dizon said. “We stand ready to cooperate fully with the Senate Committee on Public Works. We share Senator Lacson’s resolve to ensure every peso spent on public infrastructure delivers the quality and safety Filipinos deserve,” he added. Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson earlier sought an investigation into the rehabilitation of EDSA after fresh potholes emerged on newly repaired portions of the highway following recent monsoon rains. Lacson’s Senate Resolution 594 directs the Senate Committee on Public Works to conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation to review design and engineering standards and ensure accountability in public infrastructure. Lacson seeks probe on EDSA rehab after new potholes emerge

text.preview: Commuters may expect wider sidewalks and motorists will have a smoother ride throughout EDSA once its rehabilitation is finished by next year, Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon said Monday. "Buong stretch ng EDSA mula south hanggang Monumento lalaparan natin 'yung sidewalk para sa mga kababayan natin," Dizon said in an interview on Unang Balita after inspecting the EDSA-Buendia area. (On the whole stretch of EDSA from the south until Monumento, we will widen the sidewalk for our countrymen.) He also said the asphalt being used on EDSA is of good quality, at par with that being used in other countries like Japan and Korea. "Ongoing ang Phase 2 (ng EDSA rehabilitation) mula Guadalupe Orense hanggang Monumento. Ngayon nagtatrabaho tayo sa Monumento side. Kanina ininspeksiyon ko 'yung bandang Boni papunta ng Shaw Boulevard, nag-aayos na rin tayo diyan. By next year, tingin ko, tapos na ito," Dizon said. (Phase 2 [of EDSA rehabilitation] from Guadalupe Orense to Monumento is ongoing. We are working on the Monumento side. Earlier, I inspected the area [of EDSA] from Boni [Avenue] toward Shaw Boulevard as we are working there too. By next year, I think we will be finished.) articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) is seeking to impose a fine on the contractor of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program over the traffic disruption along EDSA from Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard on Sunday, August 23. In a statement on Monday, August 24, the MMDA said it is already coordinating with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to fine the contractor for allegedly failing to deploy flagmen in the area to manage traffic. The contractor could face a P50,000 fine over the violation, according to the agency. The traffic jam reportedly occurred during asphalt paving works in the area. Several sections of EDSA—a major thoroughfare that spans several cities in Metro Manila—have been undergoing rehabilitation and repair, while potholes emerged in newly rehabilitated portions following weeks of incessant heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat. The potholes formed after rainwater accumulated on the roads, according to the DPWH's initial assessment. Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the contractor to immediately repair the potholes at no cost to the government. Sen. Ping Lacson earlier called out the potholes on the newly repaired portions of EDSA and filed a resolution seeking a Senate inquiry into the rehabilitation project. The contract for Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program was awarded to Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. for P1.18 billion. The project covered Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and was completed in April 2026. Phase 2 was also awarded to Readycon in a joint venture with Dumduma Construction and Trading Corp. for P4 billion. It covers Orense Street to Monumento. text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — A resolution seeking an investigation into EDSA's rehabilitation and repair was filed on Thursday, August 13, after potholes emerged following more than a week of heavy rains in Metro Manila. Lacson cited the P6 billion budget allocated for the rehabilitation and repair of EDSA in the resolution, adding that the investigation is intended to ensure accountability. On August 10, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon inspected the EDSA Busway along Estrella Street in Makati City after potholes appeared in the area. He said the damage was caused by rainwater. The affected roads are part of Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Project. “For nearly a week, persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) rains have drenched parts of Luzon, including Metro Manila; damaging several main thoroughfares, including recently rehabilitated sections of EDSA. The presence of fresh potholes means the newly repaired avenue will already require another round of maintenance,” the resolution reads. As of June 2025, the administration has 207 Infrastructure Flagship Projects (IFPs) worth US$178 billion. Eight of these have been completed, 70 are ongoing and 23 are approved for implementation. The rest are either awaiting government approval, under the preparation stage or still in the pre-project preparation phase. In addition to the IFPs, the administration also has 3,224 infrastructure projects under the Philippine Development Plan’s 2023-2028 Public Investment Program amounting to US$ 225.1 billion. One of the big-ticket projects accomplished in 2024 is the Panguil Bay Bridge, the longest sea-crossing bridge in Mindanao. Other completed IFPs include the Expanded Plaridel Bypass Road inaugurated in October 2024 and the Samar Coastal Road Project that opened in 2023. Last November, Marcos also inaugurated the LRT-1 Cavite Extension Project Phase 1 that traverses Parañaque City and Quezon City. In 2024, the overall infrastructure disbursements were recorded at P1.55 trillion. This is equivalent to 5.8% of gross domestic product hitting last year’s target of 5.0 to 6.0%. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) also saw improvements in the country’s fixed and mobile broadband speed between January 2023 to March 2025. Despite these wins, several of the administration’s infrastructure projects face delays due to problems in Right-of-Way (ROW) acquisitions and funding. articles_for_reference_resolution.text: MANILA — The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the appearance of potholes. In a statement, Secretary Vince Dizon said the agency welcomes the proposal, as legislative oversight is “essential to ensuring transparency and protecting public funds”. He also said he has directed the DPWH National Capital Region to compel the contractor to repair all affected sections of Phase 1 at zero cost to the government, as well as to address the causes of the problem. “We are auditing contractor compliance, and if our investigation reveals substandard workmanship or negligence, we will hold those responsible fully accountable,” Dizon said. “We stand ready to cooperate fully with the Senate Committee on Public Works. We share Senator Lacson’s resolve to ensure every peso spent on public infrastructure delivers the quality and safety Filipinos deserve,” he added. Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson earlier sought an investigation into the rehabilitation of EDSA after fresh potholes emerged on newly repaired portions of the highway following recent monsoon rains. Lacson’s Senate Resolution 594 directs the Senate Committee on Public Works to conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation to review design and engineering standards and ensure accountability in public infrastructure. articles.text: MANILA — The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the appearance of potholes. In a statement, Secretary Vince Dizon said the agency welcomes the proposal, as legislative oversight is “essential to ensuring transparency and protecting public funds”. He also said he has directed the DPWH National Capital Region to compel the contractor to repair all affected sections of Phase 1 at zero cost to the government, as well as to address the causes of the problem. “We are auditing contractor compliance, and if our investigation reveals substandard workmanship or negligence, we will hold those responsible fully accountable,” Dizon said. “We stand ready to cooperate fully with the Senate Committee on Public Works. We share Senator Lacson’s resolve to ensure every peso spent on public infrastructure delivers the quality and safety Filipinos deserve,” he added. Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson earlier sought an investigation into the rehabilitation of EDSA after fresh potholes emerged on newly repaired portions of the highway following recent monsoon rains. Lacson’s Senate Resolution 594 directs the Senate Committee on Public Works to conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation to review design and engineering standards and ensure accountability in public infrastructure. As of June 2025, the administration has 207 Infrastructure Flagship Projects (IFPs) worth US$178 billion. Eight of these have been completed, 70 are ongoing and 23 are approved for implementation. The rest are either awaiting government approval, under the preparation stage or still in the pre-project preparation phase. In addition to the IFPs, the administration also has 3,224 infrastructure projects under the Philippine Development Plan’s 2023-2028 Public Investment Program amounting to US$ 225.1 billion. One of the big-ticket projects accomplished in 2024 is the Panguil Bay Bridge, the longest sea-crossing bridge in Mindanao. Other completed IFPs include the Expanded Plaridel Bypass Road inaugurated in October 2024 and the Samar Coastal Road Project that opened in 2023. Last November, Marcos also inaugurated the LRT-1 Cavite Extension Project Phase 1 that traverses Parañaque City and Quezon City. In 2024, the overall infrastructure disbursements were recorded at P1.55 trillion. This is equivalent to 5.8% of gross domestic product hitting last year’s target of 5.0 to 6.0%. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) also saw improvements in the country’s fixed and mobile broadband speed between January 2023 to March 2025. article.description: The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the
article.text: MANILA — The Department of Public Works and Highways on Friday said it welcomes the call for a Senate inquiry into the EDSA Phase 1 Rehabilitation Project following the appearance of potholes. In a statement, Secretary Vince Dizon said the agency welcomes the proposal, as legislative oversight is “essential to ensuring transparency and protecting public funds”. He also said he has directed the DPWH National Capital Region to compel the contractor to repair all affected sections of Phase 1 at zero cost to the government, as well as to address the causes of the problem. “We are auditing contractor compliance, and if our investigation reveals substandard workmanship or negligence, we will hold those responsible fully accountable,” Dizon said. “We stand ready to cooperate fully with the Senate Committee on Public Works. We share Senator Lacson’s resolve to ensure every peso spent on public infrastructure delivers the quality and safety Filipinos deserve,” he added. Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson earlier sought an investigation into the rehabilitation of EDSA after fresh potholes emerged on newly repaired portions of the highway following recent monsoon rains. Lacson’s Senate Resolution 594 directs the Senate Committee on Public Works to conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation to review design and engineering standards and ensure accountability in public infrastructure. text.preview: Commuters may expect wider sidewalks and motorists will have a smoother ride throughout EDSA once its rehabilitation is finished by next year, Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon said Monday. "Buong stretch ng EDSA mula south hanggang Monumento lalaparan natin 'yung sidewalk para sa mga kababayan natin," Dizon said in an interview on Unang Balita after inspecting the EDSA-Buendia area. article.title: MMDA eyes P50,000 fine for EDSA rehab contractor over traffic jam
article.description: The MMDA wants the contractor of EDSA rehabilitation project to pay a fine over traffic disruption caused by road asphalt paving along EDSA Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard.
article.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) is seeking to impose a fine on the contractor of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program over the traffic disruption along EDSA from Guadalupe to Shaw Boulevard on Sunday, August 23. In a statement on Monday, August 24, the MMDA said it is already coordinating with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to fine the contractor for allegedly failing to deploy flagmen in the area to manage traffic. The contractor could face a P50,000 fine over the violation, according to the agency. The traffic jam reportedly occurred during asphalt paving works in the area. Several sections of EDSA—a major thoroughfare that spans several cities in Metro Manila—have been undergoing rehabilitation and repair, while potholes emerged in newly rehabilitated portions following weeks of incessant heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat. The potholes formed after rainwater accumulated on the roads, according to the DPWH's initial assessment. Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the contractor to immediately repair the potholes at no cost to the government. Sen. Ping Lacson earlier called out the potholes on the newly repaired portions of EDSA and filed a resolution seeking a Senate inquiry into the rehabilitation project. The contract for Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Program was awarded to Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. for P1.18 billion. The project covered Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and was completed in April 2026. Phase 2 was also awarded to Readycon in a joint venture with Dumduma Construction and Trading Corp. for P4 billion. It covers Orense Street to Monumento. The affected roads are part of Phase 1 of the EDSA Rehabilitation Project. “For nearly a week, persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) rains have drenched parts of Luzon, including Metro Manila; damaging several main thoroughfares, including recently rehabilitated sections of EDSA. The presence of fresh potholes means the newly repaired avenue will already require another round of maintenance,” the resolution reads. The project was launched by the Department of Public Works and Highways in June 2025, with Phase 1 covering the repair of Roxas Boulevard to Orense Street and Phase 2 covering Orense Street to Monumento. claim.evidence_context:
"SEC. VINCE IS GREAT"
The issue of the quality of the EDSA rehabilitation project has been reopened after it was reported that several sections of the road undergoing reblocking have already developed potholes and peeling despite having been recently completed.
According to a report from 24 Oras, affected areas include several sections of the EDSA Busway and parts of Phase 1 of the road reblocking project that started on Christmas Eve of last year.
The cost of the project is estimated to reach P1.2 billion.
As a result, veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza criticized the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) under Secretary Vince Dizon.
In his social media post, he questioned why certain parts of EDSA have damaged so quickly despite the large funds allocated for the rehabilitation.
As of now, Dizon has not issued any statement regarding the criticisms and the report about the condition of some newly repaired sections of the main thoroughfare in Metro Manila.
